sources.entry: minimal-git-server - Lightweight git server with a basic CLI to manage repositories, supporting multiple accounts and running in a container. MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: A containerized minimal git server that hosts repositories over SSH and is managed through a basic command-line interface driven by a single config.yml file.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a git server inside a container, configured by one YAML file that defines multiple accounts, each with its own SSH public keys and uid. Users log in over SSH to manage repositories with a basic CLI (the README names list, create, rename and remove, among others). The same commands can be run non-interactively from scripts by invoking ssh with a command, and the repo includes a test.sh with examples. Server SSH keys are generated and persisted in a volume. Pre-built images are published to GitHub Container Registry with main, dev, latest and semver tags.
use_cases: give several users git access with separate SSH keys
script creation of git repos from automation
run a small git remote in Docker or Podman
manage git repositories over SSH from the command line
how_to_run: Create config.yml with external_hostname, external_port and an accounts list (user, uid, keys)
notable: All accounts and allowed SSH public keys are defined in a single config.yml mounted into the container
Repository management is done by SSH-ing in and running commands, so it scripts easily
Tested on both Docker and Podman
Follows semantic versioning; the major-version image tag is recommended for automatic updates
caveats: The README is brief and has a truncated config example and an unfinished 'Basic Usage' section, so the full command list is not documented
Only the three volumes described are documented; other setup details are not covered
keywords: lightweight alternative to large git forge
